rule.population: the WHOLE admitted population: every `.sql` file under the corpus root, walked with `statSync` (SYMLINK-FOLLOWING), admitted when present AND <= 1,048,576 bytes
rule.counting: NODE counts over the served build's own parse: how many times the construct's node type occurs, and in how many files
rule.reading: a count is the NEAR MISS's size, not the type's verdict: the contract decides whether the near miss IS the type, and the contract is cited in each `whyNot`

rulings.nearMiss: a TABLE PARTITION — `CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF <parent>` — a table that is a FRAGMENT of another table
rulings.whyNot: the contract (`src/ast/types.ts:164-190`) is about a library unit INCLUDING a part FILE: a part shares the library's single scope, imports nothing, and cannot be resolved as a separate module. A partition is a TABLE, it resolves as its own relation, and it is a row-level storage division — a table-level `part_of` candidate, not the file-level one the contract names.

rulings.nearMiss: a VIEW — `CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT ...` — a named relation that RENDERS a query's result
rulings.whyNot: the contract (`src/ast/types.ts:146-154`) makes the TARGET a rendered COMPONENT that a renderer constructs. A view's target is a QUERY, and the view IS a relation rather than a renderer of a component; there is no component-shaped target in the construct at all.

rulings.nearMiss: a COMMENT ON <object> — text that DECORATES the object it is attached to
rulings.whyNot: the contract (`src/ast/types.ts:137-144`) makes the SOURCE the decorated DECLARATION and the TARGET the decorator, applied by the runtime at creation. A COMMENT is text attached after the fact: it names no decorator, and the direction of the useful edge (object -> comment) is the opposite of the contract's.

rulings.nearMiss: a routine BODY — `CREATE FUNCTION ... $$ ... $$` — code MIXED INTO the routine's own scope
rulings.whyNot: the contract (`src/ast/types.ts:155-162`) makes the SOURCE a class COMPOSING a mixin into its SUPERTYPE CHAIN. A routine body is not a mixin and there is no supertype chain in it; the only SQL construct that composes members into a type's chain is the inheritance clause, which is 0 sites and belongs to `extends`.

rulings.nearMiss: a routine that RETURNS a result set — `RETURNS TABLE` / `RETURNS SETOF` — a unit PUBLISHING a named result
rulings.whyNot: the contract's export is a MODULE's named export. A SQL routine publishes a result over a CALL, it does not export a name from a module scope, and the grammar carries no export node type at all (`keyword_export` is absent from the served build's 594).

rulings.nearMiss: a DOMAIN or a base TYPE — `CREATE DOMAIN d AS <base>` / `CREATE TYPE ... (...)` — a type that CONFORMS to a base type
rulings.whyNot: the contract's implements is a type DECLARING conformance to an INTERFACE — a named contract with no body. SQL declares no interface: a domain over a base type is a VALUE RESTRICTION, not a conformance declaration, and the served build carries no implement/interface/super node type (measured: 0 of 594).
